Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate charges between 2028-06-28 and 2028-06-29

Sofia / Karthik — quick update on my side.

Preliminary hypothesis: we had a change to the aggregation scheduler on 2028-06-28 that altered the cutover for our per-tenant batching window. In normal operation we use half-open windows [T, T+W) which prevents double-counting. The new scheduler rollout briefly created overlapping boundary conditions for a small subset of tenants (multi-worker handoff), which could surface as duplicated request_ids in the billing export if replication and dedup were out of sync.

Action items I can run now:
1) Pull raw ingress events for AtlasOps for 06/28 00:00 to 06/29 23:59 and dedupe by request_id + server_instance.
2) Extract aggregation job logs for the same window — should show handoff timestamps.
3) Produce a provisional duplicate-count and a suggested credit calculation (tokens duplicated * unit price).

I'll need sign-off from Sofia before pulling full raw logs that contain request payload metadata (sensitive). If we get a sample CSV from AtlasOps with the IDs you mentioned, I can run a targeted trace first.

Ben
Sr. Billing Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate charges between 2028-06-28 and 2028-06-29

Hi Maya — final update from our investigation and proposed remediation.

Summary of findings:
- Root cause: a staged rollout of an aggregation scheduler (2028-06-28 01:18 UTC) introduced a brief overlap in batching boundaries for the multi-worker handoff path. During the handoff the deduplication index wasn't consistently checked in one of the transient worker processes.
- Impact: ~0.9% of AtlasOps' tokens for 06/28–06/29 were double-counted (we validated by matching your provided request_ids against ingress logs and comparing deduped vs raw counts).

Evidence attached: server_audit_log_snippet.txt + a sanitized CSV we generated matching your sample. Full audit traces are on the linked Drive share for your finance/audit team.

Proposed remediation / credit:
- Provisional credit: we recommend a credit of $2,420.00 which equals duplicated_token_count (12,100 tokens) * your unit price ($0.20 per 1k tokens converted; calculation shown in the linked doc).
- Operational fix: we've rolled back the scheduler change on 2028-06-29 02:05 UTC and added a stricter handoff check to avoid dedup-scopes being missed. We'll also add an automated alert for boundary overlaps.

Next steps — please confirm one of the following by reply: 
A) Accept provisional credit and apply to next invoice (July), and we’ll mark the ticket resolved.
B) Request a formal audit export (we can provide line-level evidence and the full dedupe trace) and hold for your internal review before applying credit.

If you accept (A), we'll create the credit memo and share accounting reference for reconciliation. If you choose (B), Ben will prepare the full export (requires standard NDA/data transfer agreement which we can route through the drive link).

Sorry again for the disruption — thank you for the sample file, it made the trace straightforward. Let me know if you'd like a short call (cc'ing Ben + Karthik) to walk your finance team through the logs.

— Sofia
